header: This is THE "intelligent engine" I asked for in chat (29 Sep 2026), now a HYBRID, three-tier router, refined further in chat the same day:
1. FAST PATH: the existing deterministic regex parser (parser.ts/analytics.ts, unchanged). Instant, free. I try it first for every query.

2. LEARNED-PATTERN CACHE (patternCache.ts): a template the LLM previously generalized from a real, successfully-answered query (e.g. "list all names ends with {name}"). Also fast and free: one cached DB read plus a handful of regex tests, no LLM call. It matches the SAME PHRASING SHAPE with a different name/department/designation, the way a hand-written parser rule would, except that this "rule" was derived by the LLM from real usage, not hand-coded in advance.

3. SLOW PATH: full LLM classification (intentClassifier.ts), reached only when neither of the above recognises the query at all. Its output is grounded against the same real resolution layers (designationGrades.ts, sailDepartments.ts) as everything else, and if grounding succeeds and the result looks real, its generalized template is persisted via patternCache.ts, so the SAME shape of question is answered by tier 2 next time, not tier 3 again.

This is a genuine cache in the SWR sense: a miss is slow (it hits the LLM, the "source of truth" for classification), a hit is fast, and the fast path's coverage grows on its own from real, observed usage instead of needing a new hand-written rule for every new phrasing. That was the whole point I raised in chat: no fixed number of patches ever finishes, but a self-extending cache converges toward the real, bounded vocabulary actual users produce. LEARNING NOW REQUIRES REAL FEEDBACK, NOT JUST A HEURISTIC (I refined this further in chat, 29 Sep 2026): a fresh LLM-derived template is inserted as 'pending' and is NOT matchable by anyone until a person explicitly ticks it as correct. Nothing is inferred from behaviour (dwell-time signals were removed permanently; see patternCache.ts for why). `looksLikeARealAnswer` below is only a cheap pre-filter, so I do not even create a pending row for an obvious error/empty result. It is NOT what makes a pattern trustworthy; the feedback lifecycle is.

symbols.name: resolveDeptText
symbols.sig: async function resolveDeptText(text: string): Promise<DeptGroup | null>

symbols.name: groundIntent
symbols.sig: async function groundIntent(parsed: ParsedIntent): Promise<AnalyticsIntent | null>
doc: I turn a validated ParsedIntent into a real, executable AnalyticsIntent by grounding its free-text fields against actual data. It returns null when something the person clearly mentioned (a department, a designation) can't be resolved; the caller treats that as a failed attempt, not a partial success to guess through.

symbols.name: describeGrounded
doc: Plain-language description of what a grounded (LLM-derived or cache-derived) intent will actually do. I show it under the answer so a misread question is visible at a glance (29 Sep 2026). I build it from the GROUNDED intent, what really ran, not from the model's own free-text, so it can't disagree with the results beneath it. Returns null for intents with nothing useful to say.

symbols.name: looksLikeARealAnswer
doc: I use this to decide whether a result looks like a genuine, real answer worth learning from, as opposed to an error/pending message or a hollow zero-with-no-list, which could just as easily mean the classification was subtly wrong.

symbols.name: answerEmployeeQuery
symbols.sig: export async function answerEmployeeQuery(rawQuery: string): Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Primary entry point. It has the SAME signature as analytics.ts's answerAnalytics, so the ai-search route's call site needs only a direct import swap.
